**Finding submitted: deviation on ASSIGN (Section 22.4).**

What I found across the responsive locations:

- **§22.4 (p0289)** — mutual consent requirement and the "not unreasonably withheld" standard are already present (two fallback elements met verbatim). But the successor limb is materially asymmetric: M&I may "freely assign" on merger, reorganization, sale of assets/stock/securities, or to a successor of the M&I Data Services division, while Customer's consent-free route is limited to a merger in which Customer is a party *and* where the survivor becomes an Affiliate of an institution with ≥$100,000,000 capital and surplus. A sale of substantially all assets, or a merger with a smaller acquirer, still needs M&I's consent. No written notice is required either way.
- **§21.11.B (p0284)** — on a Customer Change in Control M&I "agrees to continue to provide Services"; it caps volume (pre-change entities, prior 3-month volume +25%) but grants no termination or re-pricing right, so no walk-away trigger.
- **§11.3 (redacted; referenced in §11.1)** — appears to be a Customer termination route excused from the Termination for Convenience Fee, i.e. in our favour; not flagged.

Redline (fallback target, validated `ok:true`): a symmetrical successor carve-out for Customer replacing the $100M acquirer test, plus one short mutual written-notice sentence. I deliberately did not add an affiliate carve-out (which would conflict with the fallback's "other assignments require consent") and did not chase the preferred position, since that would require deleting M&I's negotiated free-assignment right and adding a competitor bar.
